attributes.description: opsdir-adapter-x509 (kind pki, declaration-only): plan.py (what each endpoint is asked: CRL URLs, OCSP GET requests with a SHA-1 CertID, no nonce, one serial from core revocation.probe_serial), collect.py (estate collector of observing Requests), verify.py (CRL and OCSP response parsing and signature checks: CA-signed, delegated responder with id-kp-OCSPSigning; PSS OCSP unsupported), revocation.py (importer x509/revocation replacing ou=revocation-observations). The only package depending on cryptography.
attributes.external_dependencies: ["cryptography>=50.0.2 (pyca; CRL/OCSP parsing, signature verification, OCSP request building)"]
attributes.purpose: The X.509 standards (RFC 5280 CRLs, RFC 6960 OCSP), CA-neutral: every recorded CA's revocation endpoints observed read-only and checked against the CA certificates the record holds, into the core pki domain's revocation observations

attributes.description: Each recorded CA's revocation endpoints (ou=certificate-authorities children) observed from where relying parties sit, CA-neutral (RFC 5280/6960; decision of task 548): an operator-run, read-only estate collection (opsdir-adapter-x509, importer x509/revocation) GETs every http(s) CRL / delta CRL endpoint and asks every OCSP responder (RFC 6960 A.1 GET, SHA-1 CertID, no nonce) about one certificate the CA issued; the core's observing Request keeps whatever each answers (status, body as base64, or why nothing) without failing the collection. The importer (pure, offline, the only code needing the cryptography library) verifies each answer against the record's CA certificates (signature, issuer, cRLSign; OCSP: the CA or a delegated responder it issued with id-kp-OCSPSigning) and replaces ou=revocation-observations (ciamRevocationObservation per CA, ciamEndpointObservation per endpoint: answer, this/next update, CRL numbers, signature check, signer, OCSP status). The core pki domain's pure check (revocation.py) turns unreachable, unreadable, wrongly signed, expired or stale (estate setting revocation-freshness-margin-hours) endpoints, a delta ahead of its base, and OCSP answers disagreeing with the CA's inventory into actions for the CA's owners; report revocation-endpoints.

attributes.name: run_call
attributes.purpose: Effect: (output, problem) of one collection call: Command as a subprocess (no shell; credentials only on stdin; extra env switches; failure = 'exit N: <last 600 chars of stderr, redacted>', or not installed / timeout); a workdir Command runs in a private 0700 directory and returns {relative path: text} of what it wrote under export/ (.git never read; a symlink or non-UTF-8 file maps to None, failing the collection if kept); Request as an HTTP GET (Authorization built in memory; TLS trust from the CA reference or system store); an observing Request (observe=True) via _observe: whatever the endpoint answered (HTTP error statuses too, body at most OBSERVED_BYTES) or why it answered nothing, as core.observation text dated by this host's UTC clock, never a problem

attributes.name: endpoint_entry
attributes.purpose: Importer builder: the n-th ciamRevocationEndpoint of a kind under a CA, with its URL and the CA's unexpanded template when variables remain

attributes.name: authority_of
attributes.purpose: The CA a record certificate was issued by: ciamIssuedBy listed as CA's own certificate, else issuer = CA certificate's subject, else issuer CN = CA name; None for a CA's own certificate

attributes.name: find_issued
attributes.purpose: The issued certificate matching a record certificate: fingerprint (everywhere) > serial > subject+validity (its CA's rows)

attributes.name: observation
attributes.purpose: An observing Request's output text: JSON {observedAt (ISO 8601 UTC, Z), status, contentType, body (base64, so a binary answer is kept), error}, indented, newline-terminated.

attributes.name: read_observation
attributes.purpose: (Observation, problem): an observing Request's output read back (observedAt parsed as UTC, body base64-decoded strictly, status an int or null); (None, why) when it isn't one.

attributes.name: observation_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "authority", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the CA's name"}, {"name": "at", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "GeneralizedTime"}, {"name": "state", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "complete|incomplete"}, {"name": "problems", "type": "tuple[str]", "required": false}]
attributes.purpose: The observation of the revocation endpoints of the CA named authority (ciamRevocationObservation, cn the CA's name, under ou=revocation-observations): made at `at`, complete or incomplete, with why; attributes the importer doesn't own kept.

attributes.name: endpoint_observation_entry
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "authority", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "endpoint", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the endpoint's cn"}, {"name": "kind", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "crl|delta-crl|ocsp"}, {"name": "url", "type": "str", "required": true, "description": "the endpoint's ciamEndpointUrl as recorded"}, {"name": "at", "type": "str", "required": true}, {"name": "facts", "type": "dict", "required": true}]
attributes.purpose: What one revocation endpoint (cn e.g. crl-1) of the CA named authority answered when observed at `at` at url (ciamEndpointObservation child of the CA's observation): facts {attribute of FACTS: value, or a tuple for ciamInventoryProblem; None not known}.

attributes.name: observations_group
attributes.purpose: An Imported group: ou=revocation-observations made exactly these entries (observations and their endpoints' answers, parents first by depth; the container kept).

attributes.name: observable_url
attributes.purpose: (the URL to GET, None) of a revocation endpoint, its path percent-encoded (spaces; existing escapes kept); (None, why) when it can't be observed: its URL still holds the CA's variables (description starts with issued.TEMPLATE_KEPT) or isn't http(s).

attributes.name: authority_certificates
attributes.purpose: The CA's own certificates the record holds: its ciamCaCertificate entries, else the CA certificates (chain.ca_certificates) whose subject's common name is its name.

attributes.name: probe_serial
attributes.purpose: (serial, which certificate) an OCSP responder of the CA is asked about: a record certificate the CA issued (its ciamSerialNumber, else the serial of the inventory row found for it), else the newest unrevoked certificate in the CA's inventory; (None, why) when none.

attributes.name: observations
attributes.purpose: {CA name lowercase: its ciamRevocationObservation} of every observation the record holds.

attributes.name: endpoint_observations
attributes.purpose: {endpoint name lowercase: what it answered} of one CA's observation.

attributes.name: observation_for
attributes.purpose: What an endpoint answered at its CA's last observation, or None: not observed, or observed at another URL (changed since).

attributes.name: endpoint_problems
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "d", "type": "Directory", "required": true}, {"name": "obs", "type": "Entry", "required": true, "description": "a ciamEndpointObservation"}, {"name": "margin", "type": "timedelta", "required": true}, {"name": "published", "type": "tuple[int]", "required": false, "description": "CRL numbers the CA's distribution points served"}, {"name": "rows", "type": "tuple[Entry]", "required": false, "description": "the CA inventory's certificates"}]
attributes.purpose: ((short label, text), ...) of what is wrong with what an endpoint answered: http-error/unreachable/unreadable; bad signature, other issuer, unauthorized responder, no CA certificate; expired, stale within margin, CRL without nextUpdate; delta ahead of the published CRL numbers; OCSP refused, unknown, or contradicting the CA's inventory rows.

attributes.name: judged
attributes.purpose: ((endpoint, its observation or None, problems), ...) for each crl/delta-crl/ocsp endpoint of a CA: an observable endpoint its last observation missed is a 'not observed' problem.

attributes.name: check_revocation_endpoints
attributes.purpose: Planner check: nothing when the record holds no revocation observation; else each observed CA's endpoint with a problem (judged) an action for the CA's owners (owner_label), and endpoints answering current and validly signed counted as ok. Margin from the estate setting revocation-freshness-margin-hours.

attributes.name: revocation_rows
attributes.purpose: Report revocation-endpoints (dated): one row per crl/delta-crl/ocsp endpoint of every CA: URL, observed at, answer, this/next update, CRL number (or the base a delta builds on), signature check, OCSP status and serial, state (problem labels, ok, not observed; outdated when nextUpdate is before as_of), detail (the observation's ciamInventoryProblem: why not observed, HTTP status, responder certificate) and the CA's owners.

attributes.name: observation_dn
attributes.purpose: The DN of the observation of the revocation endpoints of the CA of that name (cn=<name>,ou=revocation-observations).

attributes.name: common_name
attributes.purpose: The CN of a distinguished name as text (CN=Example CA, O=Example -> Example CA), or None.

attributes.name: serial_key
attributes.purpose: A serial number as compared: hex digits only, lowercase, without leading zeros.

attributes.name: load_certificate
attributes.purpose: The first certificate of a PEM text as an x509.Certificate, or None when it isn't one.

attributes.name: serial_hex
attributes.purpose: A serial number (int) as lowercase hex of even length, as the record writes serials.

attributes.name: key_hash
attributes.purpose: SHA-1 of a certificate's subjectPublicKey bits (RFC 6960 CertID issuerKeyHash; RFC 5280 key identifier method 1), via x509.SubjectKeyIdentifier.from_public_key.

attributes.name: name_hash
attributes.purpose: SHA-1 of a certificate's DER subject name (RFC 6960 CertID issuerNameHash when it is the issuer).

attributes.name: crl_facts
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "body", "type": "bytes", "required": true}, {"name": "cas", "type": "tuple[(Entry, x509.Certificate)]", "required": true, "description": "the CA's own certificates"}]
attributes.purpose: Facts (core revocation FACTS) of a CRL an endpoint served (DER or PEM) checked against the CA's certificates: answered with this/next update, CRL number, delta base, signature check (valid / invalid incl. key usage without cRLSign / other-issuer / no-ca-certificate / unsupported) and signer DN; unreadable when it isn't a CRL.

attributes.name: ocsp_facts
attributes.parameters: [{"name": "body", "type": "bytes", "required": true}, {"name": "cas", "type": "tuple[(Entry, x509.Certificate)]", "required": true}, {"name": "serial", "type": "str|None", "required": false, "description": "the serial asked about"}]
attributes.purpose: Facts of an OCSP responder's answer (DER): a non-successful response's status (malformedRequest..unauthorized) with the serial asked about; else certificate status, this/next update, the response's serial and the signature check (CA-signed, or a delegated responder certificate in the response issued directly by the CA with id-kp-OCSPSigning valid at producedAt; else unauthorized-responder; RSA-PSS unsupported); unreadable when it isn't an OCSP response or answers more than one certificate.

attributes.name: signing_certificates
attributes.purpose: ((record entry, x509.Certificate), ...) of the CA's own certificates (core revocation.authority_certificates) whose recorded PEM loads.

attributes.name: ocsp_request
attributes.purpose: DER of an RFC 6960 OCSPRequest about the certificate with that serial (hex) the CA certificate issuer issued: one SHA-1 CertID (name_hash, key_hash), no nonce, unsigned.

attributes.name: ocsp_get_url
attributes.purpose: The GET form of an OCSP request (RFC 6960 A.1): the responder URL (trailing slash dropped), '/', the request's base64, URL-encoded.

attributes.name: export_path
attributes.purpose: Where an endpoint's answer is in the export: <CA name>/<endpoint name>.json.

attributes.name: planned
attributes.purpose: How the observation treats one endpoint of a CA (Planned): its export path, the URL to GET (core revocation.observable_url; for OCSP the GET request URL about probe_serial's certificate over the first loadable CA certificate) or why not, and the serial asked about.

attributes.name: plan
attributes.purpose: The Planned crl/delta-crl/ocsp endpoints of every CA the record holds (CA issuers aren't observed).

attributes.name: revocation_steps
attributes.purpose: Collector steps (estate): ((export path, Request(url, observe=True)), ...) for every endpoint the plan fetches; anonymous, no credential.

attributes.name: answer_facts
attributes.purpose: Facts of one observed endpoint's answer (Observation): unreachable (error or no status), http-error (non-2xx status), unreadable (empty body), else crl_facts / ocsp_facts against the CA's certificates; an OCSP responder's facts always name the serial asked about.

attributes.name: read_revocation
attributes.purpose: Importer x509/revocation read: ou=revocation-observations made what the export (<CA>/<endpoint>.json observations) says each recorded CA's planned endpoints answered: per CA an observation (at its first endpoint's observation, else --at; incomplete when a planned endpoint is missing from the export), per endpoint its facts or not-observed with why; files not planned left out with a notice.

attributes.definition_json: {"url": "str", "headers": "((name, value), ...) no credentials", "credential": "(basic|bearer, ref, login) | (headers, ref, login, (login_header, secret_header)) | None", "ca": "ref of a PEM certificate | None", "absent": "tuple[int]", "keep": "fn(output) -> output | None", "observe": "bool: the answer, whatever it is, as an observation's JSON text (core.observation); never a failed call"}
attributes.description: An HTTP GET a collector asks opsdir to make itself (no other method); an observing one (observe=True) records whatever the endpoint answers (a revocation endpoint's binary answer as base64) or why it answered nothing
attributes.name: Request

attributes.description: An endpoint's answer as an observing Request recorded it (core.observation: observation text read back by read_observation)
attributes.name: Observation

attributes.description: One endpoint of a CA as the revocation observation plans it: what is fetched and where its answer goes in the export, or why it isn't observed
attributes.name: Planned

attributes.description: Item (b) of milestone 108 (analysis 3068). Observe each recorded CA's revocation endpoints (ou=certificate-authorities children: CRL, delta CRL, OCSP, CA issuers): for each http(s) CRL/delta CRL endpoint, a read-only fetch recording reachability, thisUpdate/nextUpdate and whether it is signed by the CA the record holds; for OCSP (RFC 6960), a status request for a record certificate the CA issued. Stale (past nextUpdate or within a margin as an estate setting), unreachable or wrongly signed endpoints become actions for the CA's owner as data. Follow the existing collector contract (Collector, evidence, least privilege, absent markers): the fetch runs as an operator-run collection producing an export the importer reads, never from inside the planner. Research the CRL/OCSP formats and Python stdlib/cryptography options first (Codex, read-only); check which crypto library the project already depends on before adding one. Design to the master before coding (it may change what the record holds: observed endpoint state).
attributes.name: CRL and OCSP endpoint observation

attributes.description: CRL/delta CRL and OCSP (RFC 5280/6960) parsing and signature checks with the libraries the project already has; collector shape; what observed state the record holds; staleness margin as an estate setting; master approves before coding.
